title: Compatible choice of natural adic purity and finite scalar comparisons

from.place: Imported Proof, Step 2 (Qbar-stage): transport is well defined by independence in finite coefficient extensions; the integral naturality and scalar square needed before rationalization (unit Step 3)

statement:
Fix a prime $p$, an integer $a\geq1$, $q=p^a$, the field $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, and an algebraic closure $k$ of $k_0$, as in [def-pur-conventions]. Fix a prime $\ell\ne p$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside a fixed algebraic closure, with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a smooth separated morphism of pure relative dimension $d\geq0$ between separated finite-type $k$-schemes, with smoothness and relative dimension as in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], finite type as in [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and separatedness as in [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Use the derived-complete integral constructible category of [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], its normalized DVR reduction towers [def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower], and the full subcategory $D^b_{ctf}(-,\mathcal O_E)$ defined by a single Tor-amplitude interval for all reductions [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. Use the integral pullback and completed tensor of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], the exceptional inverse image of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], and the twists of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. Put
$$H_E(K)=Lf_E^*K(d)[2d],\qquad G_E(K)=Rf_E^!K.$$
There is a simultaneous choice, for all finite coefficient fields $E$ and all $K\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\mathcal O_E)$, of isomorphisms $\gamma_{E,K}:H_E(K)\to G_E(K)$ having exactly the finite reductions specified in [thm-pur-adic-reconstruction], such that their components form an $\mathcal O_E$-linear natural transformation $H_E\Rightarrow G_E$ for each $E$ and satisfy the coefficient equations below. Here $H_E$ and $G_E$ are exact $\mathcal O_E$-linear functors on these integral finite-Tor categories, with exactness as in [def-weil-triangulated-category] and linearity as in [def-weil-linear-functor].

For every finite extension $E\subset F$ inside the fixed algebraic closure, write $C_{F/E,W}(K)=K\otimes^L_{\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,W}}\widehat{\mathcal O}_{F,W}$ for ordinary derived change of completed coefficient rings on $W=X,Y$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients, lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. On derived-complete inputs it is canonically identified with the strict inverse-limit integral scalar extension of [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension] by the natural isomorphism $\chi_{F/E,K}$ of [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison]. All the following comparisons are expressed for this ordinary derived-tensor presentation; their associators are its tensor associators. There are canonical exact natural comparison isomorphisms
$$a_{F/E}:C_{F/E,X}H_E\xrightarrow{\sim}H_FC_{F/E,Y},\qquad b_{F/E}:C_{F/E,X}G_E\xrightarrow{\sim}G_FC_{F/E,Y}.$$
Here $a$ is the pullback, tensor, twist and shift comparison. Use the compact-support functors $Rf_{!,E}$ and $Rf_{!,F}$ of [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support] and their canonical coefficient comparison $c_{F/E}:C_{F/E,Y}Rf_{!,E}\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_{!,F}C_{F/E,X}$. Writing $\epsilon_{E,K}:Rf_{!,E}G_EK\to K$ for the counit of the exceptional adjunction [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], the component $b_{F/E,K}$ is the adjoint transpose of the explicitly typed composite
$$Rf_{!,F}C_{F/E,X}G_EK\xrightarrow{c_{F/E,G_EK}^{-1}}C_{F/E,Y}Rf_{!,E}G_EK\xrightarrow{C_{F/E,Y}(\epsilon_{E,K})}C_{F/E,Y}K.$$ They satisfy
$$b_{F/E,K}\circ C_{F/E,X}(\gamma_{E,K})=\gamma_{F,C_{F/E,Y}K}\circ a_{F/E,K}.$$
Write $\alpha^W_{L,F,E}:C_{L/F,W}C_{F/E,W}\xrightarrow{\sim}C_{L/E,W}$ for the tensor associator on $W=X,Y$. Under the canonical identification $C_{E/E,W}\cong\operatorname{id}$ on derived-complete objects, the comparisons for $F=E$ are identities. For finite coefficient fields $E\subset F\subset L$, they satisfy
$$a_{L/E,K}\circ\alpha^X_{L,F,E,H_EK}=H_L(\alpha^Y_{L,F,E,K})\circ a_{L/F,C_{F/E,Y}K}\circ C_{L/F,X}(a_{F/E,K}),$$
$$b_{L/E,K}\circ\alpha^X_{L,F,E,G_EK}=G_L(\alpha^Y_{L,F,E,K})\circ b_{L/F,C_{F/E,Y}K}\circ C_{L/F,X}(b_{F/E,K}).$$
Under the canonical shift comparisons, $a_{F/E,K[1]}=a_{F/E,K}[1]$ and $b_{F/E,K[1]}=b_{F/E,K}[1]$. The purity square is an equality of natural transformations compatible with these unit, composition and shift equations.

source.place: Step 3, scalar-extension transitivity presupposed in passing from E to Qbar; extracted integral compatibility assertion
source.note: Agent auxiliary statement. Finite-level trace-transpose construction: SGA 4, Expose XVIII, 2.13.2 and 3.2.1--3.2.5, especially 3.2.3 (literature/sga/SGA4-expose-18_reedition.pdf). No Stacks tag states this adic compatibility. The simultaneous compatible choice is an additional assertion; it is not inferred for arbitrary lifts from pointwise reconstruction or equality of reductions.

proof.text: Choose nonnegative integers $D_X,D_Y$ bounding $\dim X,\dim Y$ by [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type], taking $0$ for an empty scheme. The compact-support bound of [lem-coef-integral-compact-support] sends a common interval $[a,b]$ to $[a,b+2D_X]$, while the exceptional-adjoint bound of [prop-coef-integral-exceptional-adjoint] sends it into $[a-2D_X,b+2D_Y]$. Thus $P_E=Rf_{!,E}$ and $G_E=Rf_E^!$ preserve the uniform finite-Tor domains, so the adjunction used below restricts to the stated full subcategories.

source.place: Unit Steps 2-3, checking the completed finite-Tor domains before coefficient passage

proof.text: The pullback and completed tensor preserve derived-complete constructible objects by [lem-pur-integral-operations-preserve-constructible], and finite pullback preserves the Tor interval by [lem-sf-pullback-tor-amplitude]. The locally free rank-one twists of [lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free] shift $[a,b]$ to $[a-2d,b-2d]$. The uniform domain is triangulated by [lem-weil-integral-ctf-triangulated].

source.place: Unit Steps 2-3, checking the completed finite-Tor domains before coefficient passage

proof.text: For $C_{F/E}$, exactness and associativity come from [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], comparison with strict scalar extension from [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison], and constructible preservation from [lem-weil-integral-scalar-extension-constructible]. The same Tor interval survives each ramified extension by [lem-pur-adic-scalar-extension-tor-bound], without assuming quotient flatness.

source.place: Unit Step 3, scalar-extension domain and associativity checks

proof.text: In the strict K-flat models of [lem-pur-integral-operations-well-defined], inverse image, tensor with a fixed twist, reduction, cone and shift are termwise compatible. The exact strict-tower derived-limit functor [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit] therefore makes $H_E$ exact; termwise scalar multiplication makes it $\mathcal O_E$-linear.

source.place: Unit Steps 2-3, exact strict limits and linearity

proof.text: Construct $a_{F/E}$ from the pullback and tensor comparisons of [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension], the twists of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed], and the shift identification, transporting through $\chi$ of [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison]. The compact-support comparison $c_{F/E}$ is [lem-pur-compact-support-integral-coefficient-comparison]. Balancing maps on K-flat representatives send $((x\otimes s)\otimes t)$ to $x\otimes st$ and $x\otimes1$ to $x$; [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] descends these identities and gives the unit, composition and shift laws for $a$.

source.place: Unit Step 3, scalar reassociations and compact-support coefficient comparisons

proof.text: Put $E_0=\mathbf Q_\ell$, $\mathbf1_{0,W}=\widehat{\mathbf Z}_{\ell,W}$ and $T_0=\mathbf1_{0,X}(d)[2d]$. By [lem-weil-constant-coefficient-objects-constructible] it is constructible, derived complete and has reduction interval $[0,0]$. Apply [thm-pur-adic-reconstruction] once to choose $g_0:T_0\xrightarrow{\sim}G_0\mathbf1_{0,Y}$ with prescribed finite reductions, and define $t_0=\epsilon_{0,\mathbf1_0}\circ P_0(g_0)$. Its twist interval is $[-2d,-2d]$; [lem-coef-integral-compact-support] with absolute bound $D_X$ gives $P_0T_0$ and interval $[-2d,-2d+2D_X]$. Counit compatibility in [prop-coef-integral-exceptional-adjoint] identifies reductions of $t_0$ with [def-pur-smooth-trace].

source.place: Unit Step 2, choosing one reconstructed unit-coefficient morphism

proof.text: For finite $E$ put $T_E=\mathbf1_{E,X}(d)[2d]$, $C_{E/0}=C_{E/\mathbf Q_\ell}$, and let $\theta_E:C_{E/0,X}T_0\xrightarrow{\sim}T_E$ be the Step 5 comparison (the twist and scalar-extension comparison $a$ at the unit, for $\mathbf Q_\ell\subset E$). Define $t_E=C_{E/0,Y}(t_0)c_{E/0,T_0}^{-1}P_E(\theta_E^{-1})$. For $K$ define $u_{E,K}$ as inverse projection followed by $t_E\widehat\otimes1$, using the order $T_E\widehat\otimes^LLf_E^*K$.

source.place: Unit Steps 2-3, scalar extension of the single integral trace

proof.text: Take $\gamma_{E,K}$ to be the adjoint transpose of $u_{E,K}$, precomposed with the canonical identification $H_EK\cong T_E\widehat\otimes^LLf_E^*K$ (twist reassociation and tensor symmetry). For a morphism $v:K\to K'$, naturality of the projection map, tensor maps and counit gives $G_E(v)\gamma_{E,K}=\gamma_{E,K'}H_E(v)$ after applying the injective adjunction Hom bijection. The same Hom bijection is additive and $\mathcal O_E$-linear because $P_E,G_E,H_E$ and the counit are linear; hence the transpose is $\mathcal O_E$-linear in morphisms. This is the elementary adjoint-transpose calculation in the additive linear categories supplied by [prop-coef-integral-exceptional-adjoint], [lem-weil-compact-support-reduction-tower-functor] and [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit].

source.place: Unit Steps 2-3, integral naturality and linearity

proof.text: At cofinal $E$-levels $er$, [lem-pur-compact-support-integral-coefficient-comparison] reduces $t_E$ to the extension of $t_{A_r}$, which is the finite smooth trace by [lem-pur-finite-universal-smooth-trace]. Reducing $u_{E,K}$ with [fix-prop-projection-formula] gives the finite counit composite [def-pur-smooth-trace], and [prop-coef-integral-exceptional-adjoint] identifies its transpose with the reduction of $\gamma_{E,K}$. For arbitrary $m$, choose $er\ge m$ and use [thm-pur-finite-reduction-of-purity]. Thus reductions are the prescribed maps from [thm-pur-adic-reconstruction], invertible by [thm-pur-finite-coefficient-smooth-purity]. If $Q$ is the cone, [lem-weil-integral-ctf-triangulated] makes it derived complete; exact reduction [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] makes every reduction zero, and [def-weil-derived-complete] plus [lem-kun-distinguished-cone-zero] gives $Q=0$.

source.place: Unit Steps 1-3, cofinal reductions and zero-cone detection

proof.text: Define $b_{F/E,K}$ as the transpose of $C_Y(\epsilon_{E,K})c_{F/E,G_EK}^{-1}$ using [prop-coef-integral-exceptional-adjoint]. Naturality follows from naturality of $c$ and the counit.
Tensor this trace identity with $C_YK$ and use the coefficient and projection compatibility of [fix-prop-projection-formula] to obtain $u_{F,C_YK}P_F(a_{F/E,K})c_{F/E,H_EK}=C_Y(u_{E,K})$.

source.place: Unit Step 3, projection compatibility of trace-valued maps

proof.text: Transpose the two sides under $P_F\dashv G_F$. Naturality of $c^{-1}$ and the definition of $b$ make the transpose of $b_KC_X(\gamma_{E,K})$ equal to $C_Y(u_{E,K})c_{H_EK}^{-1}$, while the transpose of $\gamma_{F,C_YK}a_K$ is $u_{F,C_YK}P_F(a_K)$. The preceding identity and injectivity of the adjunction Hom bijection prove the purity square. Since $a$ and both purity maps are isomorphisms, $b$ is an isomorphism.

The tensor formula of Step 5 gives the associator and identity equations for $a$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] to the three adjunctions and inverse coefficient squares $c_{F/E}^{-1},c_{L/F}^{-1}$. The mate of the pasted square is $b_{L/F,C_{F/E,Y}K}C_{L/F,X}(b_{F/E,K})$, and the composition equation for $c$ in [lem-pur-compact-support-integral-coefficient-comparison] identifies the paste with $c_{L/E}^{-1}$. This is the displayed equation for $b$; the identity extension gives $b_{E/E}=1$.

The compact-support functor is exact and has its specified shifts by [lem-weil-compact-support-reduction-tower-functor] and [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. The canonical adjunction shift comparison for $G_E$ is characterized by the counit through $\operatorname{Hom}(M,G_E(K[1]))\cong\operatorname{Hom}(P_EM,K[1])\cong\operatorname{Hom}(P_E(M[-1]),K)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(M[-1],G_EK)$.

The compact-support projection map commutes with shifting its second input, including proper and open constituents, by [lem-pur-adic-projection-shift-coherence]. Its proof uses [def-exchange-projection], the proper mate shift [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact], and exact extension by zero and its projection formula [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero, lem-cbc-extension-zero-projection-formula].

Consequently $u_{E,K[1]}=u_{E,K}[1]$ and $\gamma_{E,K[1]}=\gamma_{E,K}[1]$ by [lem-pur-adic-projection-shift-coherence] applied with $T=T_E$ and $t=t_E$; the identification $H_EK\cong T_E\widehat\otimes^LLf_E^*K$ of Step 8 commutes with the shift in $K$, the Koszul sign of moving the shift past $T_E$ (in degree $-2d$) being $(-1)^{2d}=1$. Exactness of $H_E$ and the shifted adjunction make $G_E$ exact on the finite-Tor categories. Since $c$ commutes with shift by [lem-pur-compact-support-integral-coefficient-comparison], transposing its shifted defining composite gives $b_{F/E,K[1]}=b_{F/E,K}[1]$. Applying this to the purity square proves its shift compatibility.

source.place: Unit Step 3, shift compatibility of purity and coefficient comparisons

split_report.summary: Repair of the returned split, in seventeen proof steps. Two returned auxiliary nodes were removed: the compact-support/exceptional Tor-bound node (Step 1 now cites lem-coef-integral-compact-support and prop-coef-integral-exceptional-adjoint directly) and the adjoint-transpose linearity node (now the elementary calculation of Step 8). Three statement-only prerequisites carry the remaining hidden arguments: ramified scalar-extension Tor preservation (Step 3), scalar coherence of the reconstructed traces (Step 11), and projection/adjunction shift compatibility of trace-valued maps (Steps 16-17). The item statement and hypotheses are unchanged. Maintainer review 2026-10-18: the projection-shift node no longer requires T in degree zero (its use has T=T_E in degree -2d); stale step cross-references corrected.
split_report.blueprint: Imported thm-pur-rational-and-qbar-purity Proof Step 2: independence of finite field extension; unit sk-thm-purity-transport Steps 2-3: integral construction (Steps 1-9 of the item) followed by coherent coefficient passage (Steps 10-14) and shift compatibility (Steps 15-17). The hidden Tor-domain, trace-coherence and shift arguments are carried by three cited auxiliary nodes.

tool_uses.why: Steps 7, 9, 12 and 13 use invertibility, naturality and coefficient/reduction compatibility of the compact-support projection map with constructible first input and finite-Tor second input; the purity-transport unit does not construct the projection formula.

Steps 1 and 6 use constructible preservation, a common output Tor interval and canonical finite-reduction comparison for integral compact support, with a bound for the absolute source dimension; the purity unit has no independent compact-support preservation/reduction theorem.

Steps 3, 5 and 9 use the everywhere-defined exact derived coefficient tensor and its K-flat representatives, including nonflat quotient changes; this is a module-sheaf tool rather than a purity assertion.
Step 2 uses constructible preservation and reduction formulas for integral pullback and completed tensor; the purity-transport unit does not establish these underlying operations.
Step 5 uses the natural pullback/tensor coefficient comparisons and their unit and extension-composition clauses to form a; this is an operation comparison independent of purity.
Step 4 uses its specified K-flat strict complex models for pullback and tensor to verify exactness; the purity unit does not construct those models.
Step 2 uses rank-one local freeness, derived completeness and the specified finite reductions of the Tate twist; these coefficient-sheaf properties precede the purity-transport unit.
Step 2 uses preservation of the same Tor interval at each finite level, with f separated finite type; the purity unit assumes rather than proves the finite-Tor domain of pullback.
Steps 8 and 15 use its exact linear strict-tower lift with evaluations on morphisms; an inverse system merely in the triangulated category would not suffice to prove exactness and linearity of P.
Step 6 uses the completed unit and its free degree-zero reductions to apply adic reconstruction once; this is a coefficient-object construction, absent from the transport unit.
Steps 3 and 5 identify ordinary completed-ring tensor with strict-tower scalar extension and obtain completeness of the result; the unit does not compare these two presentations.
Steps 2 and 9 need closure of the uniform finite-Tor category under shifts and cones; that categorical closure is independent of purity.
Step 3 uses constructible preservation for integral scalar extension after the ordinary tensor/strict-tower comparison; no purity argument supplies that preservation.
Steps 4, 8 and 15 use the exact total-derived inverse-limit functor on strict towers and its K-injective computation; choosing cones in a bare triangulated category gives no such functor.

Steps 1, 6-10, 13, 15 and 17 use the integral constructible right adjoint, uniform Tor bounds, and its finite-reduction unit/counit compatibility; the unit needs this underlying adjunction to transpose the trace.
Step 9 uses invertibility of the prescribed finite purity maps; this is exactly the finite smooth-purity input required by unit Step 2, not a replacement route.

Steps 1 and 6 bound the absolute dimensions of the finite-type schemes X and Y to check the compact-support and exceptional-adjoint uniform Tor domains; this generic dimension fact is not supplied by the purity-transport unit.

Step 16 uses the canonical projection mate shift identity for the separately derived proper direct-image constituent at each finite coefficient ring; this is a generic ringed-topos tool and does not assert smooth purity.
Step 16 needs exact degreewise extension by zero to pass its termwise signed tensor identity to the finite derived open projection map.
Step 16 identifies its presheaf tensor construction with the canonical derived open projection isomorphism; this open-immersion tool supplies no purity assertion.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q105-263efc7f6 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read the item, its 17 steps, the 3 new nodes and the full statement of every cited node against the master sk-thm-purity-transport Steps 1-3, with det-sp-field-extension-towers as same_as. Rechecked by hand: Step 9 (u reduces at levels er to the finite counit composite, and its transpose is gamma_{f,K} by def-pur-co-smoothness clause 2 and def-pur-smooth-purity-map; the cone vanishes) and Step 13 (both transposes equal C(u_E)c^-1). Step 14 checked: b's composition law follows from mate pasting and c's composition law. The Tor-bound node is true: when en>=m the test reduces to K_n tensor N with no flatness needed; checked for e>1. The trace-coherence node is true for any t_0. Fault 1 (E1): the projection-shift node required T to be in degree zero, but Steps 16-17 apply it to T_E=1(d)[2d], which sits in degree -2d. FIXED by allowing any T, which is true because the projection map is a morphism of exact functors in the second variable for every T; the node now also cites fix-prop-projection-formula for the invertibility of the projection map. Fault 2: Steps 7 and 14 pointed to Step 2 instead of Step 5, and the split_report summary and tool_uses step numbers were stale. FIXED in fixes/, and Steps 8 and 17 now state the H_E K = T_E tensor Lf*K identification and its Koszul sign. Batch-5 check: def-pur-co-smoothness and def-pur-smooth-purity-map are definitions and reach lem-pod-integral-pullback-composition, which is generic integral-pullback functoriality. lem-pur-compact-support-integral-coefficient-comparison reaches lem-trf-adjoint-mate, a pure lemma on conjugate adjoints. Neither is given by or part of the trace-formula or Poincare-duality proofs, so all three citations are accepted. All 20 tool_uses accepted.
